subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `openclaw notify` admin command with a typed Gateway/UI notification event, or should this be folded into existing notification/Admin RPC surfaces instead?
rationale: Current main has adjacent primitives but no exact contract, and choosing where shell-originated UI notifications belong affects core Gateway API, Control UI UX, and admin security policy.

options.title: Add narrow core notify contract
options.body: Define an admin-scoped Gateway method/event, Control UI handler, and `openclaw notify` command with explicit targeting, payload, and abuse controls.

options.title: Fold into broader WebUI notifications
options.body: Track this as a subcase of the broader notification/toast work so the command waits for the shared UI notification model.

options.title: Keep outside core for now
options.body: Require a plugin or Admin HTTP RPC extension to own host automation, after adding any missing extension API intentionally.

recommendation.title: Add narrow core notify contract
recommendation.body: Define an admin-scoped Gateway method/event, Control UI handler, and `openclaw notify` command with explicit targeting, payload, and abuse controls.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged implementation ownership is the Web Push/Gateway notification transport work that this feature would need to coordinate with.
